note: Third-party .proto corpora for the protobuf lane. NOT tracked in this repository — they are cloned protobuf-dominant repositories, so they are the one input a reader must fetch. Every entry pins an exact revision and the sparse paths that were checked out, and every probe that reads them records the revision it used, so a missing corpus is a fetch instruction rather than a mystery. Four corpora, per reviews/LANE-AUDIT-FORMULA.md's corpus-breadth dimension: the language's own reference implementation, the Google API schemas (which extend the well-known option types across files), the gRPC interop schemas (which are service- and streaming-heavy), and etcd (a proto2 real-world system). One repository's idioms are not the language, and no two of these four share a style. Stage them under `PB_CORPORA` (default <corpus-root>/bb_tests/protobuf/repos) as <name>/ checkouts with .git intact so the revision can be re-verified.
stage: for each entry: git init && git remote add origin <url> && git fetch --depth 1 origin <rev> && git sparse-checkout init --cone && git sparse-checkout set <paths> && git checkout FETCH_HEAD

corpora.name: pb-reference
corpora.role: The language's OWN reference implementation, and the strongest correctness corpus available. descriptor.proto is the file every protobuf tool reads, and the C++ test suite carries the constructs real schemas only rarely use — proto2 groups, MessageSet, editions features, parenthesised option names. A gap that hides here is a gap in the language itself. This corpus is also where the one RULED construct lives, so it is the corpus that justifies the ruling.

corpora.name: pb-googleapis
corpora.role: The canonical Google API schemas, and the corpus that exercises `extend` hardest: these files add custom options to google.protobuf.FieldOptions, MethodOptions, MessageOptions and ServiceOptions, so the extension-ownership path (members emitted onto the EXTENDED type with metadata.viaExtension, across file boundaries) is under real load rather than being demonstrated by one synthetic fixture.

corpora.name: pb-grpc
corpora.role: gRPC's own interop and example schemas. Service- and streaming-heavy, so it is the corpus that proves an rpc's request and response are told apart by position — the grammar gives both the same node type and no field name — and that `stream` is read off the tree. Imports the well-known types heavily, so cross-file resolution gets exercised.

corpora.name: pb-etcd
corpora.role: A real-world proto2 system (etcd's raft and kv schemas). Small but deliberately different: strict proto2 with `optional` labels throughout, no editions, no streaming. It is the corpus that would expose an analyzer that only understood proto3 conventions.
